paper_title: Tracing AG Codes: Toward Meeting the Gilbert-Varshamov Bound
classifications: Theory of computation → Pseudorandomness and derandomization
statement: ▶ Open Problem 4. Does there exist a prime power q = pℓ and a family of function fields Fi /Fq with ngii = Θq (1), such that each Fi of genus gi contains a Riemann–Roch space Li of degree Ti ≤ pg2i satisfying ℓi (Ti ) = Ωq (gi )?
context: This is a somewhat nonstandard regime for AG codes. Typically one works with functions of degree at least 2g, where Riemann–Roch guarantees linear growth of ℓ(T ) (indeed, ℓ(T ) = T + 1 − g for T ≥ 2g − 1). In particular, among degrees up to (1 + α)g one obtains at least αg attainable degrees. By contrast, working below g is subtler: the attainable sub-g degrees – the Weierstrass non-gaps – depend on the curve. In our TAG setting, one must therefore understand this sub-g regime. A property closely related to the latter was examined in [2, Section 4.1]. However, we are not aware of any optimal family of function fields exhibiting this behavior. For instance, in [30], the authors show that certain Riemann–Roch spaces on the Garcia–Stichtenoth tower do not satisfy this property. We formalize this as an open problem. ▶ Open Problem 4. Does there exist a prime power q = pℓ and a family of function fields Fi /Fq with ngii = Θq (1), such that each Fi of genus gi contains a Riemann–Roch space Li of degree Ti ≤ pg2i satisfying ℓi (Ti ) = Ωq (gi )? 2.1.4 Limitations and consequences of improving the bound In Section 2.1.3, we assumed that the constant appearing in the error term in Equation (2.2) is equal to 1.
